title: Contingent personalized feedback changes a pre-specified controllable state beyond static/sham feedback
purpose: Test the first physiological gate of the normal-model awareness hypothesis without treating hair growth as the immediate endpoint.

arms.B: non-contingent or sham state feedback matched for attention

primary_outcome: one pre-specified fast physiological or behavioral state with a validated measurement protocol
acceptance: C changes the pre-specified fast state more than B
B vs A separates generic attention/expectancy from feedback contingency
analysis is randomized or otherwise causally identified
outcome and analysis are frozen before unblinding
no follicle-recovery claim is made from Gate-1 success alone
failure_interpretation: If contingent feedback does not outperform sham for the pre-specified physiological state, HF01 must weaken or reject that feedback channel rather than asking the person to try harder.
next_gate: Only a successful Gate-1 state change can be tested for propagation into follicle-relevant R/F*/P/N measurements and then delayed H.
literature_boundary: HRV biofeedback/sham literature shows context-dependent physiological effects
human endocrine/immune conditioning literature shows some learnable physiological responses but does not establish a hair-follicle route
